A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching the existing appendices across renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports theoretical results and analytical regression examples. Its empirical observations are attributed to prior work; no original experiments or simulations are reported.

after.justification: Appendix B reports original synthetic regression experiments, including Bayes-gap sweeps and predictive and parameter-estimation errors in Figures 2–3.

M1.justification: The uniform-attention architecture in Definition 2 and squared-loss ERM remain unchanged. Appendix B adds a distinct experimental model, GPT-2 with positional embeddings removed, extending the models used without replacing the theoretical architecture.

E1.justification: v2 introduces actual training and evaluation on a five-dimensional, equally weighted mixture of linear regression and regression using element-wise tanh features. v1 discusses regression families analytically but evaluates no datasets or generated samples.

E2.justification: Figure 3 introduces the first empirical comparisons with Bayes (mixture) and Bayes (oracle), the latter knowing the true task family. These predictors have theoretical counterparts in v1 but were not evaluated against a trained model there.

E3.justification: Appendix B adds complete experimental protocols: N and p sweeps with 10,000 training steps, and inference experiments using 12.8 million prompts, p=15, and 200,000 online training steps. It also introduces test-sample evaluation and predictive and parameter-estimation MSE measurements; v1 has no corresponding experimental protocols.

E4.justification: Figure 2 adds sensitivity analyses of Bayes approximation to pretraining size and context length. Figure 3 adds coefficient-recovery probing to examine Bayesian parameter-estimation behavior beyond predictive accuracy. Neither empirical analysis appears in v1; the retained OOD analysis remains theoretical.

E5.justification: v2 introduces mean estimation over 1,000 Bayes-gap trials and averaging probed coefficients over 2,000 independent input-output sets. These describe sampling and averaging, not repeated training seeds. Neither version reports empirical confidence intervals, error bars, or training-run variability.

E6.justification: v2 adds all empirical results: generally declining Bayes Gap with increasing N or p, a reported gap below 0.01 after training on 12.8 million prompts with p=15, and inference curves approaching the oracle around k=3–4. Figures 2–3 provide new findings, not performance improvements over comparable v1 experiments.

T1.justification: The theorem statements, formal assumptions, lemmas, and mathematical arguments are retained across the renumbered appendices. Changes consist of minor wording, punctuation, and explanatory remarks. The mention of Bregman losses does not supply a new formal result or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal contributions retain the same risk decomposition, joint N/p generalization bounds, rapid task-family identification, and Wasserstein stability claims. The new experiments support these existing claims without redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds a prompt-learning interpretation, discusses possible extension to Bregman losses, and derives practical recommendations for model sizing, prompt length, distribution shift, and benchmark interpretation. It also interprets the new curves as rapid task identification. The adaptive-input limitation was already present in v1's Appendix B.

D1.justification: Appendix B adds the first concrete experimental recipe: task priors and noise, a 12-layer/8-head/256-hidden-size GPT-2, Adam settings, training budgets, and probing procedures. It also links the cited reference implementation and identifies its MIT license. These are newly documented experiments, not revised settings for experiments reported in v1.

R1.justification: v2 acknowledges concurrent work by Ma et al. (2025) as complementary, adds connections to prompt learning and Bregman decompositions, and explicitly positions its assumptions against earlier Bayesian analyses. Additional architecture and software citations support the experiments; the overall research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: v2 inserts an Experiments appendix and practical-implications paragraphs, expands several explanations, and adds correspondence information. Existing sections and proof narratives remain largely intact; subsequent appendix letters and cross-references are updated.

P2.justification: v2 adds two two-panel figures displaying N/p sweeps and predictive/parameter-estimation error curves, with axes, legends, and explanatory captions. Figure 1 is retained unchanged. These are localized visual additions with accompanying page reflow; neither version contains tables.

improvement.justification: Appendix B supplies useful empirical illustrations of previously theoretical claims, while the added explanations and research positioning improve accessibility. The gain is limited: the theory is unchanged, the experiments cover one synthetic mixture using GPT-2 rather than the specified theoretical architecture, and input sampling and uncertainty reporting remain incomplete. The additions strengthen the paper without establishing substantially broader validation.
